verdict.rationale: Calendly is a scheduling product, so auto-defending focus time and habits is a fair question to ask of it. The evidence only shows availability controls: buffers, custom schedules, daily limits and conflict checks before booking. These are adjacent features, not recurring focus or habit blocks that move automatically when conflicts appear. No evidence shows Calendly creating, protecting or rescheduling focus time.

support.subject: As a knowledge worker, the product auto-defends recurring focus time and habits, flexibly moving them when conflicts appear instead of dropping them
